subject: The winner 87% of users missed
preview_text: We analyzed 10,000 race predictions and found a pattern you're ignoring. It could change your picks today.
body_paragraphs: Last Tuesday at 3PM, I pulled up our data on 10,000 users. What I saw made me stop mid-bite of my sandwich. 87% of you are ignoring the one variable that separates amateurs from the guys who cash tickets. It's not jockey form. Not track condition. It's something you can spot in 10 seconds flat.

Here's the shocker: when we cross-referenced winning picks against user behavior, the losers consistently skipped the 'track bias' marker. The winners? They checked it 94% of the time. That's not luck. That's data whispering in your ear. And you're leaving money on the table by ignoring it.

Open your app right now. Scroll to any racecard for today — say, the 3:15 at Cheltenham. Look for the traffic light icon next to the track name. Green means bias toward front-runners. Red means closers. One click and you'll see our AI's confidence score adjust in real time. That's the edge.
Check it before your next bet. Then tell me if you don't see a difference. P.S. — I'm not saying gut feel is dead. I'm saying 87% of users proved it's a crutch. Be the 13%.
